Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 74, verses 1–10:

Explanation of the words:

Ya ayyuha al-muddaththir (O you who are wrapped up): That is, O you who are wrapped up in your garments, and he is the Prophet ﷺ.

Qum fa-andhir (Arise and warn): That is, warn the people of Makkah of the Fire if they do not believe and affirm the oneness of God.

Wa rabbaka fa-kabbir (And your Lord, glorify): That is, magnify your Lord above the associating of the polytheists.

Wa thiyabaka fa-tahhir (And your garments, purify): That is, purify your garments from impurities.

Wa al-rujza fa-ahjur (And abandon the idols): That is, persist in forsaking the idols.

Wa la tamnun tastakthir (And do not bestow favour seeking to gain more): That is, do not regard as a favour upon your Lord the deeds you perform for His sake in obedience to Him.

Fa-idha nuqira fi al-naqur (When the trumpet is sounded): That is, when the Trumpet is blown, the second blast.

Meaning of the verses:

The words of the Most High, ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾: that is, wrapped in his garments, and the one intended is the Prophet ﷺ. Al-Zuhri narrated, saying: revelation was interrupted from the Messenger of God ﷺ for a period, and he grieved with a great grief, so that he would run to the summits of the mountain peaks intending to throw himself down from them. Whenever he reached the top of a mountain, Jibril (peace be upon him) would appear to him and say, "You are indeed the Prophet of God," and his heart would be calmed and his soul would be at rest. The Prophet ﷺ used to relate this, saying: "While I was walking one day, I suddenly saw the angel who used to come to me at Hira' sitting on a chair between the heaven and the earth, so I was seized with terror and returned to Khadijah and said, 'Wrap me up (zammiluni)'," so they wrapped him, that is, they covered him, and God revealed: ﴿O you who are wrapped up, arise and warn, and glorify your Lord, and purify your garments.﴾ Al-Zuhri said: the first thing revealed to him was: ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created, created man from a clinging substance. Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous, who taught by the pen, taught man what he did not know.﴾ Accordingly, this divine address came after the first interruption of revelation, calling him by this beautiful title, in honour and gentleness toward him, so that he would bear the burdens of the call, and how heavy its burdens are, and who is able to bear them. They are heavy burdens. O God, Your Messenger has been aided in them, so aid me to the extent of what I do of them, even though what I do of them does not equal an ember of hellfire or a drop of rain from the sky.

O you who are wrapped in your garments, O Muhammad, our Messenger, arise and warn: there is no longer room for you to sleep and rest. Warn your people in Makkah and all of humanity beyond Makkah; warn them of the punishment of the Fire that results from disbelief and associating others with the One, the Subduer. ﴿And your Lord, glorify﴾: that is, glorify your Lord with the glorification befitting His majesty and perfection, for He is the Greatest, above whom there is no greater, and the Mighty, above whom there is no mightier. So proclaim this with your tongue, saying "God is greatest," and with your state, so do not humble yourself except to Him and do not desire except what is with Him, and magnify Him with your deeds, so do not perform any except what He has permitted you or commanded you. ﴿And your garments, purify﴾: that is, purify your garments from impurities, contrary to what your people do, for they trail their garments and do not guard themselves against their urine. ﴿And the idols, forsake﴾: that is, and the idols which your people worship, so forsake them, do not draw near to them, and persist in abandoning them. Do not bestow a gift that you have given to another seeking to gain more thereby; that is contrary to the most beautiful morals, noble dispositions and lofty manners.

And for your Lord alone, to the exclusion of all else, so be patient with all that you encounter in the course of conveying your message and spreading your call, the call to goodness and perfection. This is how God trained His Messenger at the outset of his mission. Then the following was revealed: ﴿Then when the Trumpet is sounded.﴾ The Naqur is the horn into which Israfil blows, and the sounding produces a sound, and the sound is the sound of the horn; the one intended is the second blast, the blast of resurrection and recompense. ﴿Then when the Trumpet is sounded, that will be, that day, a difficult day, hard and severe, not to be borne and not to be endured, for the disbelievers, not easy.﴾ So remind by it those you call, for reminding of it is beneficial, God willing. This is why it is among the greatest pillars of creed: when it takes firm hold of the soul, its possessor is prepared to bear every heavy burden and to spend every precious and cheap thing, and to part from family and home. Belief in God and the Last Day are the axis of faith, and upon them rests reform and guidance.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Earnestness is the mark of the Muslim; there is no laziness, no lethargy, no frivolity, no play. Whoever departs from these should examine his Islam.

2- The obligation to glorify His names and attributes, to glorify His speech and His Book, and to glorify His rites and whatever He has glorified.

3- The obligation of purity for the believer in body, garments and mosque; in eating, drinking, bedding, soul and spirit.

4- The prohibition of self-admiration: the believer should not be pleased with his deeds or praise himself through them, even if he fasts all the time and spends like a mountain and strives all his life.

5- The obligation to be patient in acts of obedience, in abstaining from sins, and in trials, submitting and being content.

**Explanation of the Words (Sharh al-Kalimat):**

*Dharni wa man khalaqtu wahidan* (﴿Leave me with the one whom I created alone﴾): That is, leave Me with the one whom I created alone and solitary, without wealth or children, for I will suffice you against him.

*Wa banina shuhudan* (﴿and sons attending﴾): That is, they attend the gatherings, their testimony is heard, and they are present most of the time and never absent.

*Wa mahhadtu lahu tamhidan* (﴿and I made preparation for him, a [good] preparation﴾): That is, I spread out for him provision in life, lifespan, children and high standing, until he was called "the fragrant herb of Quraysh" (Rayhanat Quraysh).

*Anidan* (﴿obstinate﴾): That is, stubbornly opposing, and he was al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi.

*Sa-urhiquhu saudan* (﴿I will overwhelm him with arduous torment﴾): That is, I will burden him on the Day of Resurrection with the ascent of a mountain of fire; every time he climbs it, he falls down into the Fire forever.

*Innahu fakkara wa qaddara* (﴿Indeed, he thought and calculated﴾): That is, concerning what he says about the Qur'an, which he heard from the Prophet (ﷺ), and he measured that in his own mind.

*Thumma nazara thumma 'abasa wa basara* (﴿Then he looked, then he frowned and scowled﴾): That is, he deliberated over it, then he frowned, meaning he contracted what was between his eyebrows, then he scowled, meaning his face became sullen.

*Thumma adbara wa istakbara* (﴿Then he turned away and was arrogant﴾): That is, he turned away from faith and was arrogant toward following the Messenger (ﷺ).

*Sihrun yu'thar* (﴿it is but magic transmitted﴾): That is, it is transmitted from sorcerers, such as Musaylima and others.

*Sa-usliihi saqar* (﴿I will drive him into Saqar﴾): I will cause him to enter Hell, and Saqar is one of its names; he will enter it to be burned by its fire.

*La tubqi wa la tadhar* (﴿It leaves nothing and spares nothing﴾): That is, it leaves no flesh and no sinew untouched, destroying it all, and then it returns as it was, so that the punishment continues.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 74, Verses 31–37**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Ashab al-nar* (the companions of the Fire): that is, its guardians, Malik and eighteen with him.

*Illa malaikah* (except angels): that is, We did not make them humans or jinn, so that they would not show mercy to them by virtue of kinship.

*Wa ma ja'alna 'iddatahum* (And We did not make their number): that is, that they are nineteen.

*Illa fitnatan lilladhina kafaru* (except as a trial for those who disbelieve): that is, so that they would belittle them, as Abu al-Ashuddayn al-Jumahi said, and thus increase in misguidance.

*Liyastayqina alladhina utu al-kitab* (so that those given the Book may be certain): that is, so that certainty would arise among the people of the Torah and the Gospel, through the agreement of the Qur'an with their two scriptures, the Torah and the Gospel.

*Wa la yartaba* (and that they will not doubt): that is, the People of the Book and the believers will not doubt the reality of this.

*Waliyaqula alladhina fi qulubihim maradun* (and that those in whose hearts is a disease will say): that is, the disease of hypocrisy (*nifaq*).

*Madha arada Allahu bihadha mathalan* (What does Allah intend by this as a parable?): that is, what did Allah intend by this strange number, in denial and disbelief.

*Kadhalika* (Thus): that is, like the misguidance of the one who rejects this number and the guidance of the one who confirms it; Allah misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills.

*Wa ma hiya illa dhikra lilbashar* (And it is not but a reminder to mankind): that is, the Fire is only a reminder to mankind, by which they remember.

*Idh adbar* (when it recedes): that is, when it turns back and departs.

*Idha asfar* (when it brightens): that is, when it shines and appears.

*Innaha li-ihda al-kubar* (Indeed, it is one of the greatest [calamities]): that is, Hell is one of the great afflictions.

*Nadheeran lilbashar* (a warning to mankind): that is, the punishment of Hell is a warning to the children of Adam.

*Liman sha'a minkum* (for whoever of you wills): that is, O people.

*An yataqaddama* (to advance): that is, through obedience.

*Aw yata'akhkhara* (or to lag behind): that is, through disobedience.

**Meaning of the verses:**

The words of the Most High, ﴿And We have not made the companions of the Fire except angels, and We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve﴾, were revealed in refutation of Abu al-Ashuddayn Kaladah al-Jumahi. When he heard the words of Allah, ﴿And what can make you know what Saqar is? It spares not and leaves not, a scorcher of mankind. Over it are nineteen﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 27–30], he said to the Quraysh, mockingly and derisively: "I will suffice you against seventeen, and you suffice me against two." And once he said: "I will walk before you on the Bridge (*al-Sirat*), and push ten with my right shoulder and nine with my left shoulder into the Fire, and we will pass on and enter Paradise." So Allah revealed the words, ﴿And We have not made the companions of the Fire except angels﴾, meaning: We did not make them humans or jinn, lest they show mercy to the people of the Fire. By contrast, had they been humans, they might have shown mercy to their own kind, and likewise if they had been jinn. Therefore He made them from among the angels, so there is no kinship between them and humans or jinn. By "the companions of the Fire" is meant its guardians, who are Malik and eighteen others; these are the chiefs in Hell. As for the rest of them, the expression cannot encompass them, nor even a numerical count; and how could it, when He, the Most High, has said: ﴿And none knows the hosts of your Lord except Him﴾. His words, ﴿And We have not made their number﴾, mean: that they are nineteen; ﴿except as a trial for those who disbelieve﴾, so that they would increase in misguidance and disbelief. This has indeed come to pass, for Abu Jahl, like Abu al-Ashuddayn, was tested by this number and increased in misguidance and disbelief because of what they both said.

His words, ﴿so that those who were given the Book may be certain﴾, mean: We have informed them of their number, that they are nineteen, so that those given the Book may be certain, because the Qur'an agrees with what is in their own scripture. ﴿And the believers increase in faith﴾ above their faith when they see that the Torah agrees with the Noble Qur'an as its witness. His words, ﴿and that those who were given the Book and the believers may not doubt﴾, mean: so that they will not fall into doubt or uncertainty at any time, because of the immunity they have acquired through the two Books' support of one single truth.

His words, ﴿and so that those in whose hearts is a disease and the disbelievers may say, "What does Allah intend by this as a parable?"﴾, mean: We did not make their number nineteen except so that those in whose hearts is a disease, which is hypocrisy and doubt, and the disbelievers, who manifest open disbelief, from the Quraysh and others, would say, "What does Allah intend by this as a parable?" That is, what did Allah intend by this report, so strange like parables are strange? They said this in denunciation and denial. These are reasons that He, the Most High, mentioned concerning His informing us about the guardians of Hell. Then He said, and His word is the truth: ﴿Thus Allah misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾. That is, like the misguidance of the one who rejects this number and the guidance of the one who confirms it, Allah misguides whom He wills to misguide, and guides whom He wills to guide.

His words, ﴿And none knows the hosts of your Lord except Him﴾, are a reply to Abu Jahl, who said, mocking and denying: "Does Muhammad have helpers only nineteen?" So He informed that He has hosts whose number and strength none knows except Him. It has been reported that one of them has the strength of the two weighty ones (*al-thaqalan*, that is, humans and jinn). His words, ﴿and that those who were given the Book and the believers may not doubt﴾, mean: so that they will not fall into doubt or uncertainty at any time, because of the immunity they have acquired through the two Books' support of one single truth.

That is, what did Allah intend by this report, so strange like parables are strange? They said this in denunciation and denial. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 74, verses 38–56:

Explanation of the words:

*Kullu nafsin* (every soul): that is, commanded and forbidden.

*Rahina* (held in pledge): that is, held as a pledge, seized for its deeds in Hell.

*Illa ashab al-yamin* (except the people of the right): that is, the believers, who are saved from the Fire and are in gardens of bliss, asking about the criminals.

*Wa lam naku nut'imu al-miskin* (and we did not feed the poor): that is, out of stinginess with what Allah had given them.

*Wa kunna nakhudu* (and we used to plunge): that is, into falsehood and what Allah the Exalted dislikes, along with those who plunge.

*Nukadhdhibu bi yawm al-din* (we denied the Day of Judgment): the Day of Recompense and reward, and we did not believe in any reward or punishment.

*Hatta atana al-yaqin* (until there came to us the certainty): that is, death.

*An al-tadhkirati mu'ridin* (turning away from the reminder): that is, turning away from the admonition, not listening to it and not giving it heed.

*Humurun mustanfira* (like startled donkeys): that is, as if they were wild donkeys in flight.

*Farrat min qaswara* (fleeing from a lion): that is, fleeing in the utmost flight from a lion.

*Bal yuridu kullu amri'in minhum* (rather, every one of them wants): that is, there is no deficiency in the proofs and arguments presented to them; rather, every one of them wants.

*An yu'ta suhufan munashsharah* (to be given scrolls spread out): that is, to wake up with a book from Allah, Lord of the worlds, at his head, addressed to so-and-so: believe in our Prophet Muhammad and follow him.

*Innahu tadhkira* (indeed it is a reminder): that is, an admonition and a lesson.

*Faman sha'a dhakarahu* (so whoever wills remembers it): that is, reads it and takes admonition from it.

*Huwa ahlu al-taqwa* (He is worthy of being feared): that is, He is worthy to be feared for the greatness of His dominion and the painfulness of His punishment.

*Wa ahlu al-maghfira* (and worthy of forgiveness): that is, He is worthy to forgive the repentant among His servants and the monotheists.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues establishing the belief in resurrection and recompense. Allah the Exalted says, *"Kullu nafsin"* (every soul), meaning on the Day of Resurrection, *"rahina"* (held in pledge), meaning held and confined, that is, every soul is commanded and forbidden, meaning obligated, unlike the souls of those not obligated, such as children and the insane. And His saying, *"illa ashab al-yamin"* (except the people of the right), for they have had their pledge released, and they are in gardens of bliss, asking one another about the people of Hellfire and how they are, then they connect with them while they are in the gardens of bliss and the criminals are in the midst of Hellfire. The connection occurs by seeing the person and hearing his speech, and in today's modern technology there is what has made this a reasonable matter. So they say to them, *"ma salakakum fi saqar"* (what brought you into Saqar?), that is, what caused you to enter Saqar? They answer, saying, *"lam naku mina al-musallin, wa lam naku nut'imu al-miskin, wa kunna nakhudu ma'a al-khai'in, wa kunna nukadhdhibu bi yawm al-din, hatta atana al-yaqin"* (We were not among those who prayed, nor did we feed the poor, and we used to plunge with the plungers, and we used to deny the Day of Judgment, until there came to us the certainty). So they mentioned to them the greatest of crimes, which are abandoning prayer, withholding zakat, plunging with the people of falsehood into every evil and corruption, and denying the Day of Resurrection, and that there is no reckoning and no recompense, that is, no reward and no punishment. And that they, along with these crimes that necessitate entering Saqar, did not repent of them until there came to them the certainty, which is death, for whoever dies enters the abode of the Hereafter from its threshold, which is the grave; therefore they said, *"hatta atana al-yaqin"*, that is, death. It may be asked: were there not intercessors from among the angels, the prophets, the scholars and the martyrs who would intercede? The answer is in His saying, *"fama tanfa'uhum shafa'atu al-shafi'in"* (so the intercession of the intercessors will not benefit them), that is, they had no intercession because they were atheists and criminals. And His saying, *"fama lahum 'ani al-tadhkirati mu'ridin"* (so what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder?), that is, what is the matter with these polytheists who deny resurrection and recompense that they turn away from the reminder by which they could be reminded, in the verses of this surah and others, fleeing from it? It is a strange matter: what is it that makes them turn away from it, fleeing from it? *"Ka'annahum humurun"* (as if they were donkeys) wild *"mustanfiratun farrat min qaswarah"* (startled, fleeing from a lion), that is, fleeing in the utmost flight from a lion of the lions of the tyrannical desert. Their fleeing from this call and their turning away from it is not due to a deficiency in its proofs or weakness in its argument; rather every one of them wants to be given a book from Allah ordering him to believe in and follow Muhammad ﷺ, and this is obstinacy and arrogance, and the one who has these traits is not prepared to believe under any circumstances.

This verse is like His saying: *"hatta tunazzila 'alayna kitaban naqra'uhu"* (until you bring down to us a book we can read) [al-Isra: 93]. This is the meaning of His saying, *"bal yuridu kullu amri'in minhum an yu'ta suhufan munashsharah"*. And His saying, *"kalla bal la yakhafuna al-akhirah"* (No! Rather, they do not fear the Hereafter), that is, the matter is not as they claim and assert; rather the real cause of their turning away is their not fearing Allah's punishment on the Day of Resurrection. And His saying, *"kalla innahu tadhkira"* (No! Indeed it is a reminder), that is, verily this Qur'an is a reminder; *"faman sha'a dhakarahu"*, that is, whoever wills reads it and takes admonition from it, believes in Allah and fears Him, for he will be saved and will be happy in the neighborhood of his Lord; and whoever does not will that, then for him is Saqar, and what will make you know what Saqar is. And His saying, *"wa ma yadhkurun illa an yasha'a Allah"* (and they do not remember except that Allah wills), that is, no one remembers except by the will of Allah; therefore there must be dependence upon Allah and seeking His guidance in that, for no one is independent of Allah and no one is self-sufficient without Allah; rather all are in need of Him, and His will follows His will. And His saying, *"Huwa ahlu al-taqwa wa ahlu al-maghfira"* (He is worthy of being feared and worthy of forgiving): it has been authentically related that the Prophet ﷺ explained this verse, saying: "Your Lord says: I am worthy that I be feared, so that no other god is set up with Me; so whoever fears Me and does not set up another god with Me, I am worthy to forgive him."

Guidance from the verses:

1. The release of every soul held in pledge by its earnings is faith and taqwa.

2. Clarification of the greatest crimes: abandoning prayer, withholding zakat, plunging into falsehood, and not believing in reckoning and recompense.

Explanation of the words:

*Kullu nafsin* (every soul): that is, commanded and forbidden.

*Rahina* (held in pledge): that is, held as a pledge, seized for its deeds in Hell.

*Illa ashab al-yamin* (except the people of the right): that is, the believers, who are saved from the Fire and are in gardens of bliss, asking about the criminals.

*Wa lam naku nut'imu al-miskin* (and we did not feed the poor): that is, out of stinginess with what Allah had given them.

*Wa kunna nakhudu* (and we used to plunge): that is, into falsehood and what Allah the Exalted dislikes, along with those who plunge.

*Nukadhdhibu bi yawm al-din* (we denied the Day of Judgment): the Day of Recompense and reward, and we did not believe in any reward or punishment.

*Hatta atana al-yaqin* (until there came to us the certainty): that is, death.

*An al-tadhkirati mu'ridin* (turning away from the reminder): that is, turning away from the admonition, not listening to it and not giving it heed.

*Humurun mustanfira* (like startled donkeys): that is, as if they were wild donkeys in flight.

*Farrat min qaswara* (fleeing from a lion): that is, fleeing in the utmost flight from a lion.

*Bal yuridu kullu amri'in minhum* (rather, every one of them wants): that is, there is no deficiency in the proofs and arguments presented to them; rather, every one of them wants.

*An yu'ta suhufan munashsharah* (to be given scrolls spread out): that is, to wake up with a book from Allah, Lord of the worlds, at his head, addressed to so-and-so: believe in our Prophet Muhammad and follow him.

*Innahu tadhkira* (indeed it is a reminder): that is, an admonition and a lesson.

*Faman sha'a dhakarahu* (so whoever wills remembers it): that is, reads it and takes admonition from it.

*Huwa ahlu al-taqwa* (He is worthy of being feared): that is, He is worthy to be feared for the greatness of His dominion and the painfulness of His punishment.

*Wa ahlu al-maghfira* (and worthy of forgiveness): that is, He is worthy to forgive the repentant among His servants and the monotheists.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues establishing the belief in resurrection and recompense. Allah the Exalted says, *"Kullu nafsin"* (every soul), meaning on the Day of Resurrection, *"rahina"* (held in pledge), meaning held and confined, that is, every soul is commanded and forbidden, meaning obligated, unlike the souls of those not obligated, such as children and the insane. And His saying, *"illa ashab al-yamin"* (except the people of the right), for they have had their pledge released, and they are in gardens of bliss, asking one another about the people of Hellfire and how they are, then they connect with them while they are in the gardens of bliss and the criminals are in the midst of Hellfire. The connection occurs by seeing the person and hearing his speech, and in today's modern technology there is what has made this a reasonable matter. So they say to them, *"ma salakakum fi saqar"* (what brought you into Saqar?), that is, what caused you to enter Saqar? They answer, saying, *"lam naku mina al-musallin, wa lam naku nut'imu al-miskin, wa kunna nakhudu ma'a al-khai'in, wa kunna nukadhdhibu bi yawm al-din, hatta atana al-yaqin"* (We were not among those who prayed, nor did we feed the poor, and we used to plunge with the plungers, and we used to deny the Day of Judgment, until there came to us the certainty). So they mentioned to them the greatest of crimes, which are abandoning prayer, withholding zakat, plunging with the people of falsehood into every evil and corruption, and denying the Day of Resurrection, and that there is no reckoning and no recompense, that is, no reward and no punishment. And that they, along with these crimes that necessitate entering Saqar, did not repent of them until there came to them the certainty, which is death, for whoever dies enters the abode of the Hereafter from its threshold, which is the grave; therefore they said, *"hatta atana al-yaqin"*, that is, death. It may be asked: were there not intercessors from among the angels, the prophets, the scholars and the martyrs who would intercede? The answer is in His saying, *"fama tanfa'uhum shafa'atu al-shafi'in"* (so the intercession of the intercessors will not benefit them), that is, they had no intercession because they were atheists and criminals. And His saying, *"fama lahum 'ani al-tadhkirati mu'ridin"* (so what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder?), that is, what is the matter with these polytheists who deny resurrection and recompense that they turn away from the reminder by which they could be reminded, in the verses of this surah and others, fleeing from it? It is a strange matter: what is it that makes them turn away from it, fleeing from it? *"Ka'annahum humurun"* (as if they were donkeys) wild *"mustanfiratun farrat min qaswarah"* (startled, fleeing from a lion), that is, fleeing in the utmost flight from a lion of the lions of the tyrannical desert. Their fleeing from this call and their turning away from it is not due to a deficiency in its proofs or weakness in its argument; rather every one of them wants to be given a book from Allah ordering him to believe in and follow Muhammad ﷺ, and this is obstinacy and arrogance, and the one who has these traits is not prepared to believe under any circumstances.

This verse is like His saying: *"hatta tunazzila 'alayna kitaban naqra'uhu"* (until you bring down to us a book we can read) [al-Isra: 93]. This is the meaning of His saying, *"bal yuridu kullu amri'in minhum an yu'ta suhufan munashsharah"*. And His saying, *"kalla bal la yakhafuna al-akhirah"* (No! Rather, they do not fear the Hereafter), that is, the matter is not as they claim and assert; rather the real cause of their turning away is their not fearing Allah's punishment on the Day of Resurrection. And His saying, *"kalla innahu tadhkira"* (No! Indeed it is a reminder), that is, verily this Qur'an is a reminder; *"faman sha'a dhakarahu"*, that is, whoever wills reads it and takes admonition from it, believes in Allah and fears Him, for he will be saved and will be happy in the neighborhood of his Lord; and whoever does not will that, then for him is Saqar, and what will make you know what Saqar is. And His saying, *"wa ma yadhkurun illa an yasha'a Allah"* (and they do not remember except that Allah wills), that is, no one remembers except by the will of Allah; therefore there must be dependence upon Allah and seeking His guidance in that, for no one is independent of Allah and no one is self-sufficient without Allah; rather all are in need of Him, and His will follows His will. And His saying, *"Huwa ahlu al-taqwa wa ahlu al-maghfira"* (He is worthy of being feared and worthy of forgiving): it has been authentically related that the Prophet ﷺ explained this verse, saying: "Your Lord says: I am worthy that I be feared, so that no other god is set up with Me; so whoever fears Me and does not set up another god with Me, I am worthy to forgive him."

2. Clarification of the greatest crimes: abandoning prayer, withholding zakat, plunging into falsehood, and not believing in reckoning and recompense.

4. The deviation of a person returns to the weakness of his faith in resurrection and recompense.
